openings.claim: The known spacer function may establish repeatable lateral clearance for hatch seating without increased downward corner pressure.
openings.delta: Replace dependence on marker-only centering with opposed corner spacer faces carried by removable brackets made from the supplied strips. Drill or notch strips only; use bolts and rubber pads to seat bracket pairs against the rim. No strap function is proposed.
openings.prediction: Against the ordinary rival of manually centering the untreated hatch, bounded spacer clearance should reduce displacement from the stipulated 4 mm to at most 1 mm under 20 N. If corner lift persists without increased downward pressure, lateral spacers have not resolved that disturbance. These are predictions, not observations.
openings.probe: First dry-fit the four strips as two opposed corner brackets, checking clearance in both lateral axes, rim engagement and removal. Proceed only if the assembly can resist sideways loading without modifying the fixture or obstructing the open aperture. Allocate ten closure/pull trials to ten spacer opening cycles, including the right-contact card on final closure; use two untreated rival trials, one disturbed. Record position, 20 N displacement, corner lift, visible seal damage and full reopening time, including bracket removal onto the tabletop. Limit fabrication to ninety minutes and observation to twenty minutes. Failure to complete these measurements defeats the probe, regardless of stopping on time.
assumptions: Rim geometry permits padded bolted brackets and opposing spacer faces; that geometry is unspecified.
Four strips and six bolts suffice to establish clearances and react 20 N without permanent deformation; capacity is unmeasured.
Brackets can be removed within thirty seconds while all loose parts remain recoverable and the marked opening stays unobstructed.
The disturbed right contact does not invalidate lateral seating or tear the seal. Any failed outcome defeats this configuration; no constraint relaxation is authorized.

assessment: A spacer-only candidate with an ordinary rival and finite comparison. Feasibility depends on unprovided rim geometry and bracket capacity; this is a probe proposal, not deployment or demonstrated performance.
